title: Solving sin(2*theta) - cos(theta) = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find all solutions to the equation \sin 2\theta - \cos\theta = 0 in the interval 0 \le \theta \le 2\pi.

steps.title: Expand sin(2*theta) and Factor
steps.explanation: Replace sin(2*theta) with 2*sin(theta)*cos(theta) and factor out the common factor cos(theta).
steps.why: Factoring rather than dividing by cos(theta) ensures we do not lose roots where cos(theta) = 0.

steps.title: Solve cos(theta) = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Set the first factor equal to zero to obtain the quadrantal angles pi/2 and 3*pi/2.
steps.why: On the unit circle, the x-coordinate is zero at the top and bottom points (0, 1) and (0, -1).

steps.title: Solve 2*sin(theta) - 1 = 0 on [0, 2*pi]
steps.explanation: Set the second factor equal to zero: sin(theta) = 1/2, which has solutions pi/6 in Quadrant I and 5*pi/6 in Quadrant II.
steps.why: By the zero-product property, the union of the two solution sets gives all four roots.
